When the mixed air dewpoint remained below 50 °F and ambient, return air and space conditions allowed, the HEDS optimization code switched to mode 8 – cooling without dehumidification. It remained in this state during the HEDS operation throughout the remainder of the evaluation period. • Due to the stark difference in performance between periods (1) and (2), and given that the remaining operating modes do not have dehumidification needs, performance comparisons are only made using the mode 8 operating period for the VAV HEDS operation. • Without a dehumidification call, the CRC coil has no impact on the energy usage of the system, as seen in periods (2) and (4), during which the CRC_water_reheat is 0. • At low air flow rates, the VAV reheat coil had to run to compensate for the heat loss during M&V operating period (2). However, during M&V operating period (4), the heat gain from the fan at full power (18.5 kW) was enough to entirely cover the heat losses from the system, so no additional reheat was needed at the zone terminals. 21 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. • During M&V operating periods (2) and (4), the cooling coil is rarely turned on since the HEDS controller does not request dehumidification, as discussed above, and the supply temperature setpoint is maintained above the zone temperature by the HEDS controller. This allows recirculated air to reduce the amount of heat required at the reheat coils to control the zone temperatures. In the corresponding baseline modes (3 and 5), the supply temperature setpoint remains in the 50-55 °F range. This difference is the main reason for significant chilled water consumption during baseline modes even though the overall Space_load and Misc_load are negative. This result shows that almost all the chilled water thermal power provided during M&V operating period (3) and about 75% of chilled water usage in M&V operating period (5) are not satisfying a required load, i.e. the chiller operation is unnecessary and results in a large amount of wasted energy during these times. As evidence, the chilled water energy is almost identical to the reheat energy in period (3): 86,929 vs 88,167 W, respectively. In addition, during operating period (4), the HEDS supply air temperature (HEDSsupplyAir) is always higher than the average space temperature MeanAirTemp, which clearly shows that it is effectively in a heating, not cooling, mode. While the simple control strategies employed in both CAV operating modes (3) and (4) are typical of most legacy systems, the wasted energy is significant. While it is possible to change setpoints during a season when dehumidification is no longer needed, this requires regular monitoring, and random and/or frequent weather changes will not generally result in operational changes if there is no impact on occupant comfort. This real-world operational data reinforces the need to equip HVAC systems with optimization systems that can effectively evaluate internal and ambient conditions and automatically adjust system setpoints to minimize energy waste.
